goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/vms.json (48 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Access control (IAM), Tags, Diagnose and solve problems, Resource visualizer, Connect, Networking, Settings, Availability + scale, Security, Backup + disaster recovery, Operations, Monitoring)
Backend: ARM Microsoft.Compute virtualMachines over Vyomi's compute backend (grep providers/ core/ for azure vm): list/create/start/stop/delete, disks, NICs
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/vms.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.vms.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape
note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

depth_targets.title: Disks (OS disk, data disks)
limitations: OS disk and data disks are modelled as an embedded field on the virtual machine resource (properties.storageProfile), the same shape the create wizard writes, rather than standalone Microsoft.Compute/disks resources — so 'Attach existing disk' (which would need a standalone Disks console to pick from) is an honest gap. 'Create and attach a new disk' and detaching a data disk are real.

depth_targets.title: Networking (network interface, inbound/outbound port rules)
limitations: The virtual machine's network interface (Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces) and, when a network security group is attached, its inbound/outbound rules (Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/securityRules) are real ARM resources and real CRUD — the same engine the Network security groups console uses. Load balancing, Application security groups and Network manager are an honest gap (this lens does not model those resource types), and Public IP address is not modelled (always '--').

depth_targets.title: Connect (SSH command)
limitations: The displayed SSH command is built from the virtual machine's real admin username and its network interface's private IP address, but Vyomi does not open a real SSH session, and Bastion is not modelled (no public IP address is modelled either, matching azure.vms.networking).

depth_targets.title: Identity (system-assigned managed identity)
limitations: The identity.type flag round-trips through ARM exactly as configured, but Vyomi never issues a managed-identity token or honours it on any other resource's access checks.

depth_targets.title: Auto-shutdown schedule
limitations: The schedule, time zone and notification settings are stored on the virtual machine and returned exactly as configured, but Vyomi never runs a scheduler — the virtual machine is not actually powered off at the scheduled time.

depth_targets.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

depth_targets.title: Export template
limitations: Only the ARM Template tab is generated from the live resource; Bicep and Terraform export are not modelled.

depth_targets.title: Access control (IAM)
limitations: Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments is only simulated at subscription scope, so role assignments/roles/deny assignments/classic administrators scoped to a single virtual machine are an honest gap.

depth_targets.title: Run command
limitations: Guest command execution requires a live VM agent; virtual machines are metadata-only in Vyomi (no runtime backing them in-browser), so scripts are never actually run.

depth_targets.title: Insights, Alerts, Metrics, Diagnostic settings, Logs, Connection monitor, Workbooks
limitations: Azure Monitor metrics/alerts/diagnostic settings and Network Watcher connection monitor for virtual machines are not modelled.

depth_targets.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Resource visualizer, Bastion, Load balancing, Application security groups, Network manager, Extensions + applications, Operating system, Configuration, Advisor recommendations, Availability + scaling, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Backup, Disaster recovery, Updates, Inventory, Change tracking, Tasks, Resource health, Boot diagnostics, Performance diagnostics, Reset password, Redeploy + reapply, Serial console, Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: These console tools need a live guest agent, hypervisor telemetry or resource types this lens does not model.
